hero.title: Collections
intro.0: The everyday containers real code reaches for. Write and run each one: build a List<T> and grow it, walk it with foreach, index into it, fill it with your own objects, then map keys to values with a Dictionary.
task.1.title: Make a list
task.1.context:
An array has a fixed size. A `List<T>` grows as you add to it. The `<T>` says what it holds:

- `List<string>` - a list of text
- `List<int>` - a list of whole numbers

`Add` appends one item; `Count` is how many it holds.
task.2.title: Walk a list with foreach
task.2.context: `foreach` hands you each item of a list in turn - no index to manage. A list can also be filled inline with `{ ... }` instead of repeated `Add`s.
task.2.goal.0: Walk `pets` with a `foreach` and print `name + " is here!"` for each.
task.2.goal.1: The output should be Rex is here!, then Whiskers is here!, then Bubbles is here!.
task.3.title: Read by position
task.3.context:
Items in a list have a position, counted from `0`. Read one with square brackets:

- `queue[0]` is the first item
- `queue[queue.Count - 1]` is always the last

The first index is `0`, not `1`.
task.3.goal.0: Print `queue[0] + " is first"`, then the last one via `queue[queue.Count - 1] + " is last"`.
task.3.goal.1: The output should be Pingu is first, then Waddles is last.
task.4.title: A list of your own objects
task.4.context: A list can hold your own objects, not just strings. `List<Cat>` holds whole `Cat` objects, each with its own fields. Inside a `foreach`, each `cat` is one object you can read from.
task.4.goal.1: `foreach` over them, printing `cat.Name + " guilty: " + cat.KnockedSomethingOver`. Output: Mittens guilty: True, then Smudge guilty: False.
task.5.title: Look up by key
task.5.context: A `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` maps a key to a value. The angle brackets hold two types: the key type, then the value type. `legs["puppy"]` both sets and reads the value for that key.
task.5.goal.0: Make a `Dictionary<string, int>` called `legs`, store `"puppy"` = 4 and `"chicken"` = 2.
task.5.goal.1: Print `legs["puppy"] + " legs"`. The output should be 4 legs.
task.6.title: Check before you read
task.6.context: Reading a key that was never stored fails - there is no value to hand back - so check first. `ContainsKey` returns a `bool`: `true` if the key is there, `false` if not. Guard the lookup with it.
task.6.goal.0: Use `legs.ContainsKey("snake")` in an `if`: print `legs["snake"] + " legs"` when present, otherwise `"no legs!"`.
task.6.goal.1: `"snake"` was never stored, so the output should be no legs!.
task.7.title: Count what matches
task.7.context: Loop a list and tally the items that meet a condition: start a counter at `0`, then raise it inside the loop when the test holds. This is the manual shape; LINQ later does the same in one line.
task.7.goal.0: Count the `true` values in `goodBoys` into `int treats`, then print `treats + " treats for " + goodBoys.Count + " dogs"`.
task.7.goal.1: Three of the four are good boys, so the output should be 3 treats for 4 dogs.
task.8.title: Collections recap
task.8.summaryIntro: Collections hold many values at once. These are the everyday containers you will reach for.
task.8.summaryItems.0.title: List<T> -
task.8.summaryItems.0.text: a growable, ordered collection; `Add` to it, read `Count`, index with `[i]`.
task.8.summaryItems.1.title: foreach -
task.8.summaryItems.1.text: visit each item in turn, no index needed.
task.8.summaryItems.2.title: List of objects -
task.8.summaryItems.2.text: a list can hold your own types, each with its own fields.
task.8.summaryItems.3.title: Dictionary<TKey, TValue> -
task.8.summaryItems.3.text: map a key to a value and look it up by key.
task.8.summaryItems.4.title: ContainsKey -
task.8.summaryItems.4.text: check a key exists before reading it, to avoid a failure.
task.8.summaryItems.5.title: Tally with a loop -
task.8.summaryItems.5.text: count matches by hand; LINQ will shorten this next.
task.8.summaryClose: Next in this track: the data shapes that fill these collections - properties, enums, structs and records.
concept.pr-list.def: A row of values that grows and shrinks - add items, index into it, and walk it - unlike a fixed-size array.
concept.pr-dictionary.def: A store that maps keys to values, so you look an item up by its key instead of its position.
